label: Factor radius
title: The factor of a closed rule has radius at most 2 on the image, and the sixteen rule-200 cases are explained by idempotence
kind: Exact audit of factor locality under five non-linear observations, with a theorem half and a census half
summary: Under the idempotent observations 200 and 4 the factor of every closed rule is the observation composed with the rule on the image, so its radius is at most 2; the sixteen rule-200 residual rules sit at exactly 2 and everything else at most 1. Under the non-idempotent observations 232, 32 and 22 every ring-independent closed rule has radius at most 1. The one exception is rule 223 at ring 6 under 22, closed at that ring only, whose factor needs the whole ring.
takeaway: A factor's locality radius tells whether a closure belongs to the local dynamics or to the ring: the only radius-3 cell is the only finite-ring closure in the census.
